R0007_and_R0031_clause_2.finding: ReplayVerificationService::compareExpectedAndActual already calls compareField() for import_status, promote_status, promoted, and pointer_switched (lines 1217-1220 at review time), each reading from actual['context']['actual_import_promote_context'], which is genuinely computed from the real run row (request_mode/terminal_status/publishability_state/bars_rows_written/is_current_publication -- confirmed by reading the assignment block directly, not derived from the expected side). compareField() skips comparison entirely when the expected value is null. Confirmed by direct inspection: B18ReplayComparisonExhaustivenessTest's expectedReplayResult() builder never included import_status/promote_status/promoted/pointer_switched keys in expected_run_context at all -- neither the baseline nor any of the 13 pre-existing perturbations, nor either import-only test's overrides -- so every existing test left these three comparisons permanently skipped. This is real, correctly-implemented code with zero test coverage, not an executable defect.

R0031_clause_1.finding: MarketDataEvidenceExportService::buildRunSummary computes request_mode/import_status/promote_status/promoted/import_promote_boundary purely via deriveImportStatus()/derivePromoteStatus(), both confirmed by direct reading to be pure functions of the already-fetched $run row and the already-computed $requestMode/$promoted -- neither issues a query or takes a repository parameter. Confirmed by grep: zero existing test references import_promote_boundary, deriveImportStatus, or derivePromoteStatus at all.

R0031_clause_3.finding: Already PROVEN prior to this unit via appendImportPromotionPolicyMismatches() and its guard pair (test_an_import_only_expectation_is_not_satisfied_by_a_run_that_promoted / test_an_import_only_expectation_against_an_unpromoted_run_raises_no_promotion_mismatch). Not re-derived in this unit; reused as the negative guard for R0031's proof-basis entry.

R0080.finding: MarketDataEvidenceExportService::isReadableRun() already requires terminal_status=SUCCESS AND publishability_state=READABLE AND CoverageGateStateNormalizer::normalize(coverage_gate_state)=PASS (confirmed by direct reading). Every existing test with coverage_gate_state=FAIL also had terminal_status=HELD, so the coverage clause's own necessity was never isolated -- a broken or a correct coverage clause would have produced an identical test outcome in every existing fixture.
